svg.title: Orchestrator-workers: your code wrote the fixed list, the model wrote the per-product one
svg.desc: The same launch step run on two products. A fixed list of three standard deliverables sits in the code and produces three workers for every product, drawn once because it never varies. Below it, a planner model call reads each finished listing and names the extra deliverables that product needs. A sit-stand desk carrying compliance, pricing and freight flags gets three extras and three workers. A phone case with no flags gets an empty plan and no workers at all. The code path, the cap and the call site are identical in both lanes, so the worker count is a property of the input rather than of the program.
svg.text: Same step, same code. Count the workers.
A flowchart draws the same boxes either way. The difference is where the list came from.
THE FIXED HALF · YOUR CODE WROTE THIS LIST
the same three for every product
THE DYNAMIC HALF · THE MODEL WRITES THIS LIST, PER PRODUCT

g.text: Three workers, then none, from the same call site. Your code wrote neither number.
your code · same result every run
data in flight, not a decision
